info.description:
# Introduction
Welcome to the Moveo API. The API allows you to create Virtual Assistants and connect them with different channels such as Facebook, Viber, Web Widget as well as talk to any backend or external service.
The API is designed according to REST principles. It uses JSON in request bodies and requires that the `content-type: application/json` header be specified for all such requests. The API will always respond with an object. Depending on context, resources may be returned as single objects or as arrays of objects, nested within the response object.
## API Path Versioning
The API paths are versioned. The current and latest version for API paths is `v1`, as seen in `https://api.moveo.ai/api/v1/...`.
## Account Slug
Most API requests require an `account_slug` query parameter. This slug identifies your specific Moveo.AI account. You can typically find your account slug within your Moveo.AI dashboard or from your account administrator. Ensure this parameter is included in your requests where specified.
## API Host
Moveo is available in the following regions. The API host is specific to the region.
* Europe        | https://api.moveo.ai
* United States | https://api.us-central.moveo.ai
* Brazil        | https://api.sa-east.moveo.ai
## Authorization
Moveo supports two primary authentication methods:
1.  **API Keys**: These are static keys provided to you for server-to-server authentication.
2.  **JSON Web Tokens (JWTs)**: These are typically used for user-delegated authentication.

You should include your authentication credential in the `Authorization` header. - For JWTs, use the `Bearer` scheme: `Authorization: Bearer <YOUR_JWT_TOKEN>` - For API Keys, use the following scheme: `Authorization: apikey <YOUR_API_KEY>`

### API Key Types
When creating an API key, you must select one of the following types which determines the scope of access:
*   **`manage`**: For management operations. Grants access to endpoints under brains, broadcasts, campaigns, collections, desks, plugins, and roles.
*   **`use`**: For sending messages only. Restricted to session, message, and classify endpoints.
*   **`analytics`**: For reading analytics data through the Analytics GraphQL API. It grants no access to the endpoints in this reference.
Each endpoint in this documentation specifies which API key type(s) it supports.
## Pagination
All paginated endpoints support cursor-based pagination.

Cursor-based pagination is a common pagination strategy that avoids many of the pitfalls of offset–limit pagination. It works by returning a pointer to a specific item in the dataset. On subsequent requests, the server returns results after the given pointer.

The default page size is 100 objects. To use a different page size, use the `limit` query parameter.
To change the attribute by which results are sorted, use the `sort` query parameter. Each endpoint supports different sorting attributes.
### Total Count Information
By default, paginated responses do not include the total count of all items for performance  reasons. To include the total count in the pagination response, add `verbose=true` as a query  parameter. When enabled, the `pagination` object will include a `total` field with the complete count of all items matching the query filters.
**Example:** - `GET /v1/desks/{desk_id}/brains?limit=10` - Returns pagination without total - `GET /v1/desks/{desk_id}/brains?limit=10&verbose=true` - Returns pagination with total count
## Rate Limits
Moveo APIs are subject to rate limiting. If the rate limit is exceeded Moveo may return a `429 Too Many Requests` HTTP status code. We apply rate limits to prevent abuse, spam, denial-of-service attacks, and similar issues. Our goal is to keep the limits high enough so that any application using Moveo as intended will not encounter them.

To help manage your API calls, the following headers are typically returned with each API response:
- `X-RateLimit-Limit`: The maximum number of requests allowed in the current time window.
- `X-RateLimit-Remaining`: The number of requests remaining in the current time window.
- `X-RateLimit-Reset`: The time (in UTC epoch seconds) when the current window resets.

When calling the Moveo API, you should implement `429` retry logic using exponential backoff and jitter.
## Request Size Limits
The Moveo API imposes a 10mb request size limit on HTTPS.
## Errors
Moveo uses standard HTTP status codes to communicate errors. In general, a `2xx` status code indicates success while `4xx` indicates an error, in which case, the response body includes a JSON object with a `code`, `message`, and `extra` field containing more details. Multiple errors can only be included in a `400 Bad Request`. A `5xx` status code indicates that something went wrong on our end.

Example Error Response:
```json
 {
  "code": "unauthorized",
  "message": "No authorization token was found",
  "extra": {}
 }
```

**Common Error Codes:**
*   `unauthorized`: Authentication credentials missing or invalid.
*   `permission_denied`: Authenticated user lacks permission for the action.
*   `validation_error`: Request input failed validation. `extra` field often contains details.
*   `resource_not_found`: The requested resource does not exist.
*   `invalid_request`: General request format issue.

post.description:
Send an outbound message to initiate a conversation with a user via WhatsApp, SMS, RCS, or Email.

**Session Reuse Behavior:**
- If an **open** conversation exists for this user on the same integration → returns `409 Conflict` with the existing `session_id`
- If a **closed** conversation exists → a standalone send reuses user context from that conversation (request context overwrites)
- If no conversation exists → creates a new session

**Campaign-linked send:**
Pass `campaign_id` and `subscriber_id` together to continue an existing campaign instead
of creating a standalone send. The campaign must be in progress and `external_id` must
match the subscriber's phone or email. The send is recorded as a sender on that campaign,
so its receipts land in the subscriber events and the campaign journey. A linked send uses
the subscriber's context; only request `context` overrides it.

**Response Status:**
- `201 Created`: Message queued successfully. The `status` field indicates:
  - `processed`: Message delivery confirmed within 5 seconds
  - `pending`: Message queued but delivery not yet confirmed

Permissions - `desks.read` and `conversations.create`. API keys - `manage`.
A campaign-linked send also needs `campaigns.write`, and an MCP token is refused.

status.description: Whether message delivery was confirmed within timeout

Schedule a message for future delivery (30 seconds to 14 days ahead) in an open conversation. The payload follows the conversation's channel, resolved from its integration: WhatsApp takes a `template`, while SMS and RCS take a plain-text `{ text }` body. Email and voice conversations are not supported. At the scheduled time the message is delivered in the original conversation, or skipped silently when it was cancelled, the conversation is no longer open, or the session has expired — it never opens a new conversation. Any reply from the contact cancels all pending scheduled messages for the conversation. WhatsApp template body placeholders must be positional (`{{1}}`..`{{n}}`).

post.description:
Creates a contact. The `phone` is normalized to E.164 and `email` is lowercased before storage; those normalized values are also indexed in `contact_identities` so a later inbound message on the same number or address resolves to this contact instead of creating a duplicate. An unparseable phone returns 400. If the phone or email already belongs to another contact in the account, the request is rejected with 409.

Permissions - `contacts.write`. API keys - `manage`.

when taken). Without the `name` parameter, returns the total count for generating suggested

put.description:
Updates a contact. The `phone` is normalized to E.164 and `email` is lowercased before storage. Changing either keeps `contact_identities` in sync — the previous value is retired and the new one indexed — so the identity index never goes stale. An unparseable phone returns 400. If the new phone or email already belongs to another contact in the account, the request is rejected with 409 and nothing is changed.

Permissions - `contacts.write`. API keys - `manage`.

get.description:
Returns every phone/email/external_id/psid identity linked to the contact, sorted by creation date (oldest first). Deleted identities are excluded.

Permissions - `contacts.read`. API keys - `manage`.

put.description:
Adds or links a phone/email/external_id identity for the contact. Identities dedup within the account on (type, value), not on contact_id, so three outcomes are possible: 201 when a new row is created and linked to this contact, 200 when the value is already linked to this contact, and 409 when the value already belongs to a DIFFERENT contact in the account (no_auto_merge — the row is not relinked; the caller decides whether to merge contacts or use a different value). Re-adding a previously deleted value revives the same identity row (200), preserving any consent recorded against it.

Permissions - `contacts.write`. API keys - `manage`.

200.description: The value was already linked to this contact

201.description: A new identity row was created and linked to this contact

409.description: The value already belongs to a different contact in this account. A soft-deleted identity still reserves its (type, value) for the original contact — deleting an identity does not free the value for other contacts.

delete.description:
Soft-deletes an identity. The row is stamped deleted and stops appearing in the contact's identity list, but it is retained so any consent recorded against it — including opt-outs — is preserved and stays enforced. Everything the campaign Performance tab renders in a single fetch: the recovery funnel, the KPI tiles and the daily PTP series. There is no per-channel breakdown.
The funnel and the tiles are generic arrays in display order, so one renderer serves every campaign type — a `payment_recovery` campaign returns long arrays plus `daily_ptp`, any other type returns a 2-stage funnel, a single metric and no `daily_ptp` key. Debt entries are gated on the campaign's `type`, not on whether its subscribers have linked debts. Promise metrics are produced by the agentic (NBA) flow, so they stay 0/null on non-agentic campaigns; right-party metrics can be populated on any campaign, since contact resolution also marks channel-vouched identities verified. Values with no data source in v1 are omitted from the response rather than returned as permanent nulls; a returned null means the value is not measurable for this campaign, which for a rate means its denominator was 0. Every rate is a 0-1 fraction (0.4 = 40%) rounded to 4 decimals; `ppa` is money, rounded to 2. Money is deduped per debt and summed across every currency the campaign's debts use. `currency` is the single ISO 4217 code those debts share, ignoring blank ones; it is null when they mix currencies, are all blank, when the campaign has no debts, or when it is not `payment_recovery`.
Served from a short-lived cache rather than recomputed on every request, so the numbers are a bounded approximation and can be a few minutes behind.

put.description:
Permissions - `campaign.write`. API keys - `manage`.

Add new subscribers or update existing ones. If replace=true query parameter is provided,
removes all existing subscribers before adding new ones.

replace=true is rejected with 400 for an agentic campaign that is already in_progress
when the request carries subscribers: the removed audience would return as new rows
and be contacted a second time. Stop or cancel the campaign first, or add subscribers
without replace. An empty subscribers array with replace=true is a pure delete and
is still allowed.

A campaign may hold debts in only one currency. Each upload compares the campaign's
existing debt currencies against the batch and rejects the whole request with 400
subscriber.campaignCurrencyConflict if more than one distinct currency would result,
and the message names the currencies involved. Blank currency values are exempt, and
the comparison is case-insensitive and trimmed. A replace=true call unlinks the
campaign's existing debts first, so it can move the campaign to a new currency.

CampaignAnalytics.description: Campaign performance analytics, as two generic arrays so one renderer serves every campaign type. **Array order is display order** — render left to right as returned and do not sort. `nullable` numbers mean "not measurable", as opposed to a measured 0; for a rate that means its denominator was 0. Rates are 0-1 fractions (0.4 = 40%) rounded to 4 decimals; `ppa` is money, rounded to 2. Debt entries are returned only when the campaign's `type` is `payment_recovery` — a marketing campaign that happens to carry linked debts gets the short arrays, because those debts are typically shared with other campaigns. The response carries no campaign type and no labels: the client already has the campaign object and owns the translated labels.

funnel.description: Ordered recovery funnel, aggregated across every channel. Stage keys in order: `attempts`, `responded`, then — `payment_recovery` only — `right_party_contacts` and `promises`. Stages 1-2 read `campaign_subscribers` directly with no identity filter; stages 3-4 are restricted to repliers with a verified, non-wrong-party identity, so promises <= right_party_contacts <= responded <= attempts holds by construction. The stages come from separate concurrent queries, so a write landing mid-recompute can transiently break it. The design's "Self-reported paid" stage is not returned: Dialog emits no such signal, so there is nothing to report (MOV-17770).

rate.description: Drop-off INTO this stage — this stage's value over the previous stage's. Always null on the first stage, which nothing precedes.

metrics.description: Ordered KPI tiles. `stopped` is always present. The rest are `payment_recovery` only, in this order: `rpc`, `debt_amount`, `total_ptp_amount`, `total_ptp_count`, `ppa`, `promises`, `disputes`, `rpc_rate`, `ptp_rate`, `dispute_rate`. `debt_amount` comes from the uploaded debts and `rpc` / `rpc_rate` from replies plus identity verification, so all three are populated on any campaign. Everything else — the ptp_status-derived entries, `disputes` (`debt_disputed`) and `stopped` (the `'stopped'` lifecycle value) — is written only by the agentic (NBA) paths and stays 0/null on non-agentic campaigns. The design's "Effectiveness" rate is not returned (MOV-17770).

key.description: `stopped` — subscribers whose campaign lifecycle ended in 'stopped'. `rpc` — right-party contacts. `debt_amount` — sum of current_balance across distinct debts. `total_ptp_amount` — sum of promised amounts; null when none are populated. `total_ptp_count` — distinct people who promised, same value as the `promises` funnel stage. `ppa` — average promise size; its denominator is the count of promises that actually CARRY an amount, which is deliberately not exposed, so total_ptp_amount / total_ptp_count is the wrong guess. `promises` / `disputes` — promise-bearing and disputed DEBTS, deduped by debt; a person with three promised debts counts three times here and once in the funnel, and neither is the numerator of a rate below. `rpc_rate` — rpc / responded. `ptp_rate` — promising right-party people / rpc, so people over people; NOT recomputable from the `promises` metric. `dispute_rate` — disputing right-party people / rpc; the subscriber count behind it has no exposed entry.

config.description:
Integration-specific configuration settings. The structure varies by integration type.

For WhatsApp integrations, you can update fields like:
- `display_phone_number` (string, optional): Human-readable phone number (e.g., "+1 940-642-3857")
- `session_timeout` (number): Session timeout in seconds
- `prefilled_message` (string): Default message text
- `waba_id` (string, optional): WhatsApp Business Account (WABA) id
- `voice_integration_id` (string or null, optional): ID of a `whatsapp-voice` integration on the same desk. Omitting it keeps the stored pairing; `null` clears it.

For Instagram/Facebook (Meta) integrations:
- `ignore_story_interactions` (boolean, optional): when true, a first message that is a story reply or story mention is ignored and no conversation is created. Applies to both Instagram and Facebook (story mentions exist only on Instagram). Absent/false preserves the current behavior.
- `is_coexistence` (boolean, optional, Instagram only): when true, a human reply sent from the Instagram app hands the session over to a human. Absent/false preserves the current behavior.
- `coexistence_timeout` (integer, optional, Instagram only): minutes, 1 to 10080, that a session stays with the human after an app reply. Absent means 10080 (7 days).
- `coexistence_reset_text` (string, optional, Instagram only): text, 1 to 64 characters, that a human sends from the app to give the session back to the bot. Absent means `/reset`.

For Sunshine Conversations (sunco) integrations:
- `switchboard_release_enabled` (boolean, optional): when true, switchboard control is released when a session expires. Required by Zendesk marketplace bots. Set false for legacy Smooch-widget instances, which do not support releaseControl and use passControl plugins instead. Omitting the field on an update preserves the stored value; to change it, GET the integration, merge the key into the returned config, and PUT the full config back.

For Genesys Cloud (genesys) integrations, the external human-chat provider a desk selects via `chat_integration_id`:
- `region` (string): Genesys Cloud region key, e.g. `eu-central-1` (which maps to the `mypurecloud.de` API host). Unknown regions are rejected at relay time, not here.
- `open_messaging_integration_id` (string): the Open Messaging integration id the conversation is opened against.
- `oauth_client_id` (string), `oauth_client_secret` (string): client-credentials pair. Needs both the `messaging:integration:view` and `conversation:message:receive` scopes; queue routing alone does not grant the second.
- `webhook_secret` (string, optional): HMAC secret for the agent-reply webhook. An integration with no secret currently has its deliveries accepted unverified — set it to close that.
- `default_queue_id` (string, optional), `inbound_flow_id` (string, optional): routing targets read by the Architect flow.
- `session_timeout` (number, optional): session timeout in seconds.
- `agent_avatar` (string or null, optional): https URL, up to 4096 characters. When set, replaces every agent's own avatar on replies. `null` clears it.

`oauth_client_secret` and `webhook_secret` are redacted on read like every other secret field, so a GET-merge-PUT round trip would write the mask back. Send them explicitly when changing them, and omit them otherwise.

For voice integrations (web-voice, telnyx-voice, twilio-voice, whatsapp-voice):
- `livekit` (boolean, optional): when true, the call is relayed through the LiveKit SFU instead of the legacy media path. Omitting the field on an update preserves the stored value; to change it, GET the integration, merge the key into the returned config, and PUT the full config back.

For Twilio Voice and Telnyx Voice integrations:
- `voice_psid_field` (string, optional): which part of an inbound SIP call identifies the caller. The caller identity keys the session and the contact, and it fills the user's phone when it is an E.164 number. `From` uses the SIP From. An `X-` header name, for example `X-Caller-ID`, uses the value of that header (the name match ignores case). A call without that header, or with a value over 256 characters, falls back to the SIP From and gets no phone, so a PSTN call to that integration gets no phone either. Twilio forwards only `X-` headers, so any other name has no effect. Empty keeps the SIP From. On Twilio Voice, a SIP From then fills no phone. On Telnyx Voice, Telnyx sends a SIP caller as a plain number, so that number fills the phone as on a PSTN call, even when it is the dialer's number. On an update, an absent `voice_psid_field` keeps the stored value, so send an empty string to clear it. Campaign calls do not change.

For Web (webchat) integrations:
- `voice_integration_id` (string or null, optional): ID of a `web-voice` integration on the same desk. Omitting it keeps the stored pairing; `null` clears it.
- `inactivity_timeout` (number, optional): minutes of visitor inactivity before the widget asks whether the visitor is still there. Accepts 0, which turns the prompt off, or 3 to 30. Omit it for the default of 10. Note the unit - `waiting_time_threshold` is in seconds.
- `resume_timeout` (integer, optional): minutes, 0 to 1440. When a visitor reopens the widget and the conversation has been quiet for at least this long, the widget sends the hidden opener `defaultresumemessage` so the AI agent can greet the returning visitor. Absent or 0 turns it off, which is the default. Turn it on only for an AI agent that handles `defaultresumemessage`; any other agent answers the opener with its fallback.
- `close_minimizes_window` (boolean, optional): when true, the header close button only minimizes the panel and keeps the conversation, so the visitor can never end it from there. Absent or false means close offers to end the conversation as well as minimize the panel. Whether a rating survey follows an end is still `show_survey`'s decision.
- `widget_alignment` (string, optional): `bottom-right`, `bottom-left`, `top-right`, `top-left`. `right` and `left` remain valid as aliases of the two bottom corners.
- `launcher.type` (string, optional): `bubble`, `bubble-sparkle`, `help`, `feedback`, `question`.
- `widget_position` (string, optional): `livechat`, `embed`, `popup`. `fullpage` is no longer accepted; the widget never supported it.
- Removed: `launcher.icon_url`, `launcher.text` and `launcher.padding` are dropped from the stored config. No widget code ever read them. Sending them still succeeds - the keys are stripped, not rejected - so drop them from your calls. Custom launcher artwork comes from `bubble_image`.

Every field is optional and nullable: null, blank/whitespace strings, and an empty categories array are all normalized to absent before validation, so a console posting its whole form state never fails on untouched inputs. Blank category rows are dropped rather than rejected. After that normalization at least one authoring field (name, description, type, categories) must remain, so a wholly blank draft, or one carrying only prev_recommendation, returns 400. Every constraint below therefore applies only to a field that survived normalization; a machine validator cannot express the gate, so the minimums are omitted here.

BrainChange.description:
A single change between two AI agent versions.
`kind` decides which payload fields are present:
`scalar` carries `from`/`to`, `text` carries `stats` and `hunks`,
`structural` carries `size` only (the body is never inlined, and it is also
what you get when a text field is too large to diff),
`moved` carries `from_index`/`to_index`,
and `secret` carries no payload at all — it says a credential changed, never what it is.

path.description: Slash-separated path into the exported AI agent, for example `dialogs/Greetings/nodes`. A segment taken from user text is JSON Pointer escaped (`~` as `~0`, `/` as `~1`), so a dialog named `Sales/EU` reads as `dialogs/Sales~1EU` and the value goes straight back into the `path` query parameter.

size.description: Serialized length of the omitted body, in characters.

truncated.description: True when the text budget dropped later hunks for this field.

then re-request with `path` to drill into one subtree.
A credential change (webhook token, MCP server config) is reported as a `secret`
change carrying only its path — the value is never returned, and the diff does not
descend into the field.

channel_type.description: The messaging medium. Auto-derived from channel for most integrations. Overridable only for flexible integrations (custom, front, zendesk, sunco). For other integrations, any provided value is ignored and the system derives it from the channel.

metadata.description: Optional per-request model overrides used by the console's Test panel. Honored only for console Test-panel requests (`channel: test` authenticated with a console session, not an API key); API-key callers and any other channel have these fields ignored and the brain's model strategy is used. For an eligible test request an override wins over the brain's model strategy for this message only. `language_model_id` and `language_model_alias` are mutually exclusive.

reasoning_effort.description: Reasoning effort for the overriding model. Without a model override, pins the Moveo default model at this effort.

SessionEnqueueRequest.description: A message, or a move with no message. Only a component token can send `integration_id` or a `switch_trigger` other than `message`. Any other caller gets 403.

integration_id.description: The integration the message arrived on. When it differs from the integration the session is on, the session moves to it before the message is answered, as long as it is an active integration on the session's desk. A refused move never drops the message.

channel_type.description: The channel type the person arrived with on `integration_id`. Only a flexible integration (custom, front, zendesk, sunco, zendesk_support) keeps it. Without it, a first move to a flexible integration gets that integration's default channel type.

switch_trigger.description: Why the session moves, with no message, in the session's queue. `user`: the person tapped "switch to text" or "back to voice" in the widget. `call_ended`: a call ended and the session goes back to `integration_id`. `continuation`: the person opened a continuation link.

channel_type.description: Coarse channel tier. Derived from `channel` when a provider is set; sending a value that contradicts the provider is rejected unless the integration is multi-channel (custom, front, zendesk, sunco, zendesk-support).

channel.description: Provider the simulated session runs as (carried on the session source and visible to the agent as `sys-channel`). `null` runs as the `test` channel.

starting_context.description: Initial session context seeded when the simulated session is created, merged over the synthetic visitor defaults. Nest values under the usual top-level keys (`user`, `global`, `channels`). Top-level key names must start with a letter, digit or underscore, and may then also contain dashes, so a dotted key such as `user.display_name` is rejected - send `{"user": {"display_name": "Maria"}}` instead. Capped at 32 KB serialized.

schedule_frequency.description:
Run this simulation on a shared managed schedule. Picking
`weekdays`, `weekly`, or `monthly` attaches the simulation to the
single managed schedule for that frequency on the brain (creating
it on the canonical cron if it doesn't exist yet). `null` means
the simulation is only triggered manually.

Change the managed-schedule membership. Setting a new value moves
the simulation onto that frequency's managed schedule; setting
`null` detaches it and leaves the simulation unscheduled.

schedule_id.description: Schedule that produced this run; `null` for manual runs.

duration_seconds.description: completed_at − started_at, in seconds. `null` while the run is in-flight.
